text:
incident-bot: PAGE FIRED -> severity: P1 | symptom: inference-queue backlog > 120s p99 | service: runtime-gpu-pool-1

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert #INC-12034 triggered (unacked) -> paging alex, meera

alex: acked. I'm on it. grabbing context from metrics now.

meera: ack. on phone for the next 20.

jonas: seeing a spike in enqueue_latency and worker_queue_length on CI cluster; autoscaler isn't adding nodes. kubectl logs show node-provisioner timeouts.

alex: steps: 1) confirm autoscaler state 2) check cloud quota/errors 3) if stuck, manual scale up GPU pool 4) mitigate traffic (route to dedicated pool / smaller model variant).

sam: i can help with cloud console. i'm checking GCE quota and recent provisioning errors.

alex: running:
```
kubectl get hpa -n runtime
kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=inference-worker -o wide
```
HPA shows desired 0 -> 12 but min nodes = 12 and cluster autoscaler hasn't created nodes.

meera: i see a lot of `ImagePullBackOff` on new node bootstrap logs in cloud. might be a private registry auth failure for the gpu node image.

sam: cloud console shows repeated failed instance creation: `403: accessNotConfigured` for compute.images.get to our service account. IAM role change from yesterday possibly rolled out.

alex: that would block autoscaler from adding nodes. escalating to infra-iam. meera, can you open quick ticket and ping infra-iam?

meera: opened INC-12035 and pinged @infra-iam in #eng-infra. they replied, investigating service account key rotation. ETA unknown.

jonas: mitigation idea: spin up a temporary GPU node pool using a different service account that still has image pull perms, then shift the nodeSelector for burst workloads. I can prepare a patch to nodepool-k8s.yaml.

sam: i can create the temporary pool, but we should avoid long-lived compromise. prepping command: `gcloud compute instance-templates create gpu-temp --image-project=public-images --image=container-vm` then `gcloud container node-pools create gpu-temp-pool --cluster=runtime-cluster --num-nodes=4 --node-taints=workload=burst:NoSchedule`

alex: good. before that, can we triage customer impact? metrics team: increase in 5xx for hosted/generation endpoints?

jonas: yes - hosted API 5xx rate up from 0.04% -> 2.1% in last 10m. A few customers reporting timeouts / retries. Most traffic is queuing; tail latency hitting 30s+ for some requests.

meera: adding a temporary fallback: change route for free-tier to `gpt-small-quant` (lower memory, lower latency) to reduce pressure. That will reduce quality but reduce queue. Ops change will be quick.

alex: do it. also enable aggressive request-circuit for heavy clients so we don't blow the queue. meera, please post the exact rollout command when you run it.

meera: running rollout now: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/routes/rollout -d '{"route":"hosted:free-tier","model":"gpt-small-quant","strategy":"immediate"}'` -> response: 202 accepted.

pagerduty: INC-12034 acknowledged by alex at 2024-05-12T18:22:47Z

sam: temp node pool creation started; first instances provisioning. logs show containers pulling from `public-images` ok. kubernetes should register new nodes in ~3-5m.

jonas: new nodes are Ready. reconciling pods; autoscaler still stuck but we have capacity. shifting burst pods via label selector.

alex: routing change + temp nodes in place. queue backlog dropped from p99 125s -> 28s in 7 minutes. 5xx rate falling. customers on hosted free-tier now ~stable.

meera: infra-iam confirmed service account key rotation caused image access failure. they're rolling fix to restore compute.images.get permission to the gpu-node-sa. ETA 30m.

jonas: note: we still have a backlog of long-running requests. increasing tokenization read timeouts for workers to avoid repeated failures. applied config change: `kubectl set env deployment/inference-worker TOKENIZE_TIMEOUT=45s -n runtime`

sam: monitoring pod restarts and GPU utilization. looks good.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step 4 executed: emergency scaling to temp pool. Step 7 (notify customers) pending.

alex: summary for postmortem: root cause = IAM/service-account permission change blocked node provisioning -> cluster autoscaler unable to scale -> queue backlog and elevated 5xx. Mitigations: temporary GPU node-pool using public image, route fallback to smaller model, manual timeout adjustments.

meera: contacting account execs for impacted customers; support msg drafted and queued.

jonas: oncall handoff in 45m. i'll stay until infra-iam confirms permanent fix and autoscaler healthy.

alex: good. i'll update incident channel and set status page to degraded for runtime API. keeping pager open until autoscaler shows healthy for 30m.

pagerduty: INC-12034 -> status: acknowledged -> responder: alex -> escalations: none.

incident-bot: NOTE: investigation window captured and attached to the thread.

meera: infra-iam pushed fix, permissions restored at 18:57:12Z. provisioning calls succeed now.

sam: autoscaler reconciled and added nodes to desired state. new nodes are coming up; HPA back to expected. queue p99 back under 10s.

alex: marking incident as mitigated. leaving notes for postmortem and follow-ups: - add alert gating for node-provisioner IAM errors - automated advertise fallback pool - add playbook for temp node-pool creation.

jonas: handing off to night oncall (sam) in 30m for monitoring.

sam: acknowledged handoff. monitoring for 1h then close if stable.

alex: resolved for now. will file postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
